questions.question:
Which of the below statements is/are incorrect?
Statement 1: Longitude directly determines the temperature of ocean waters.
Statement 2: Ocean currents influence ocean water temperature by transporting warm and cold water masses.
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is incorrect. Longitude does not directly affect ocean water temperature. Factors determining ocean water temperature include:
  • Latitude – affects solar radiation received
  • Land-water distribution – affects heat absorption
  • Ocean currents – transport warm and cold water masses (Statement 2 is correct)

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the Coriolis force?
questions.option_1: It deflects the wind to the right in the north and left in the south.
questions.option_2: It is directly proportional to the angle of altitude
questions.option_3: Deflection is less when the wind is high
questions.option_4: It is absent at the equator.
questions.solution:
Option 3 is incorrect. The Coriolis force deflection is greater when wind speed is higher, not less.

Key facts:
  • Deflects wind right in Northern Hemisphere, left in Southern Hemisphere
  • Maximum at poles, absent at equator
  • Acts perpendicular to pressure gradient force
  • Affects both winds and ocean currents

questions.question:
Which of the below statements is/are correct?
Statement 1: The Torrid Zone lies between the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) and the Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S).
Statement 2: The Frigid Zones are located between the Tropics and the Arctic/Antarctic Circles.
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • Torrid Zone – between Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) and Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S) – receives direct sunlight, high temperatures year-round.
  • Frigid Zones – located between Arctic Circle (66.5°N) and North Pole, and between Antarctic Circle (66.5°S) and South Pole. They are the coldest regions.
  • Temperate Zones – located between the Tropics and the Arctic/Antarctic Circles.

questions.question: Which is the Standard Meridian of India?
questions.solution: The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30' E. It passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh and also crosses Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question:
Which of the following sets of statements are correct about Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?
A. The ITCZ is a broad trough of low pressure in equatorial latitudes.
B. This is where the northeast and the southeast trade winds converge.
C. The ITCZ is the equatorial trough normally positioned about 5°N of the equator and remains there throughout the year.
D. The ITCZ moves over to the plane of Ganga in Summer.
questions.solution:
A, B, and D are correct.
  • A: ITCZ is a broad trough of low pressure in equatorial latitudes – correct.
  • B: Northeast and southeast trade winds converge here – correct.
  • C: ITCZ does NOT remain at 5°N throughout the year; it shifts seasonally – incorrect.
  • D: ITCZ moves over the Ganga plain in summer (July) – correct.
Seasonal shifts in ITCZ affect rainfall patterns, creating wet and dry seasons in the tropics.

questions.question: During October-November, the apparent movement of the sun is towards the _____.
questions.solution: During October-November, the Sun appears to move towards the South. This period from June 21 to December 22 is called Dakshinayan. From December 22 to June 21, the Sun moves north (Uttarayan).

questions.question:
Match the following waterbodies with the locations they separate:
List I (Channel)List II (Separates)
A. 8° Channeli. Andaman Islands and Nicobar Islands
B. 9° Channelii. Minicoy and Maldives
C. 10° Channeliii. Minicoy & Lakshadweep main group
D. 11° Channeliv. Amindivi Islands & Cannanore Islands
questions.solution:
Correct matching:
  • 8° Channel – separates Minicoy and Maldives (A–ii)
  • 9° Channel – separates Minicoy from Lakshadweep main group (B–iii)
  • 10° Channel – separates Andaman Islands and Nicobar Islands (C–i)
  • 11° Channel – separates Amindivi Islands and Cannanore Islands (D–iv)

questions.question: The southern part of India lies in the _________ belt.
questions.solution: The southern part of India lies in the warm belt. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India. Southern parts, being closer to the Equator, experience high temperatures year-round. Northern parts lie in the warm temperate zone.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India is NOT crossed by the Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N)?
questions.solution: Kerala is NOT crossed by the Tropic of Cancer. The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.question: On which of the following two dates does the equinox fall?
questions.solution:
Equinox falls on 21 March (Spring Equinox) and 23 September (Autumn Equinox). On these dates, the equator receives vertical rays of the Sun, and day and night are equal.

  • 21 June – Summer solstice in Northern Hemisphere, Winter solstice in Southern Hemisphere; Sun directly over Tropic of Cancer.
  • 22 December – Winter solstice in Northern Hemisphere, Summer solstice in Southern Hemisphere; Sun directly over Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.question: From the north most to south most point of India, what is the extent of India?
questions.solution:
The north-south extent of India is approximately 3,214 km.

Other extents:
  • East-West extent: 2,933 km
  • Land frontier: 15,200 km
  • Coastline: 7,516.6 km
  • Northernmost point: Indira Col
  • Southernmost point (mainland): Kanyakumari
  • Southernmost point (including islands): Indira Point (Great Nicobar)

questions.question: What is the zone between the arctic circle and north pole called?
questions.solution: The zone between the Arctic Circle (66°33'48.7" N) and the North Pole (90° N) is called the Frigid Zone (specifically the North Frigid Zone). It covers about 4.12% of Earth's surface and is the coldest region.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Isochrones are lines joining points located at equal travel time from a common centre.
2. Isohalines are lines connecting points of equal temperature in the ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct.
  • Isochrones – lines joining points with equal travel time from a common centre – correct.
  • Isohalines – lines connecting points of equal salinity, not temperature – incorrect.
  • Isotherms – lines of equal temperature.

questions.question: 1° latitude is equal to approximately ______ km.
questions.solution: 1° latitude is approximately equal to 111 km. This distance decreases slightly toward the poles and increases slightly toward the equator due to Earth's shape.

questions.question: What is the primary reason for the asymmetrical distribution of continents and oceans across the Earth's surface?
questions.solution: The primary reason is seafloor spreading and plate tectonics. Earth's continents are fragments of the supercontinent Pangaea that have drifted, collided, and rearranged due to tectonic plate movement. This process, driven by seafloor spreading at mid-ocean ridges and subduction at trenches, has resulted in the current uneven arrangement (land-heavy Northern Hemisphere, ocean-dominated Southern Hemisphere).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Arabian Sea, located in the North Indian Ocean, covers an area of about 3.86 million square kilometres.
2. The Arabian Sea has higher salinity due to high evaporation and low influx of fresh water.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Both statements are correct.
  • The Arabian Sea covers approximately 3.86 million sq km in the North Indian Ocean.
  • It has higher salinity due to high evaporation rates and low freshwater influx.
The North Indian Ocean also includes the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest crustal plate on Earth with an area of over 103,000,000 km²?
questions.solution:
The Pacific Plate is the largest crustal plate, covering over 103,000,000 km². It is the largest oceanic plate.

Plate Tectonics Theory (McKenzie, Parker, Morgan, 1967): Earth's lithosphere is divided into 7 major plates: Antarctic, North American, South American, Pacific, India-Australia-New Zealand, African, and Eurasian plates.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Peninsular Plateau of India was earlier a part of the continent Africa.
2. The Peninsular Plateau of India was earlier a part of the continent North America.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution: Only Statement 2 is incorrect. The Peninsular Plateau of India was part of the supercontinent Gondwana, which included Africa, South America, Australia, and Antarctica. After breaking from Gondwana, the Indian subcontinent drifted north and collided with Eurasia, forming the Himalayas.

questions.question: In the context of water bodies, Neap Tides occur:
questions.option_1: when the earth, moon and sun line up in a straight line
questions.option_2: when the sun and moon are on the opposite sides
questions.option_3: when there is so much interference by continents
questions.option_4: when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other
questions.solution:
Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other. During neap tides, gravitational and centrifugal forces are divided, resulting in:
  • Lower high tides than average
  • Higher low tides than average
Spring tides occur when the Sun, Moon, and Earth are aligned in a straight line, producing higher high tides and lower low tides.

questions.question: Which of the following is a landlocked Salt Lake in South-West Asia between Israel and Jordan?
questions.solution:
The Dead Sea is a landlocked salt lake between Israel and Jordan. Its salinity is 340 grams per litre, with a density of 1.240 kg/L, making swimming similar to floating.

  • Caspian Sea – world's largest saltwater lake by volume
  • Aral Sea – between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan

questions.question: Which ocean is encircling the continent of Antarctica and extends northward to 60 degrees south latitude?
questions.solution: The Southern Ocean encircles Antarctica and extends northward to 60°S latitude. It is the newest of the world's five oceans, officially designated by the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) in 2000.

questions.question: The name of the strait between the Pacific and Arctic oceans, separating the Chukchi Peninsula of the Russian Far East from the Seward Peninsula of Alaska, is the:
questions.solution:
The Bering Strait separates the Chukchi Peninsula (Russia) from the Seward Peninsula (Alaska), connecting the Pacific and Arctic Oceans.

  • Davis Strait – between Greenland and Baffin Island (Canada)
  • Florida Strait – between Florida Keys and Cuba
  • Strait of Messina – between Sicily and Calabria (Italy)

questions.question: In 1596, who suggested in his work 'Thesaurus Geographicus' that the continents of the earth were not always located in their present positions?
questions.solution: Abraham Ortelius, a Dutch mapmaker, proposed in his 1596 work Thesaurus Geographicus that continents were once joined. This laid groundwork for continental drift theory, later fully developed by Alfred Wegener (1912), who suggested all continents formed a single landmass called Pangaea surrounded by ocean Panthalassa.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the ocean floor?
questions.solution:
Deep sea shelf is NOT a part of the ocean floor. Ocean floor features include:
  • Continental shelf – submerged edge of a continent
  • Continental slope – extends seaward from the shelf
  • Abyssal plain (deep sea plain) – flat region at 3,000-6,000 meters depth
  • Other features: submarine canyons, deep ocean trenches, guyots, seamounts, mid-ocean ridges

questions.question: The thermocline layer is the ______ layer of the ocean.
questions.solution:
The thermocline layer is the second layer of the ocean (Mesopelagic Zone). Ocean layers:
  1. Epipelagic Zone – surface to 200m
  2. Mesopelagic Zone (Thermocline) – 200-1,000m, twilight zone
  3. Bathypelagic Zone – 1,000-4,000m, midnight zone
  4. Abyssopelagic Zone – 4,000-6,000m, near freezing
  5. Hadalpelagic Zone – 6,000m to bottom (Mariana Trench)
